HelpInstallNotifications.meta_description: Install Migrennity for faster access and more reliable notifications, plus step-by-step setup tips for iPhone/iPad, Android, and desktop.
HelpInstallNotifications.title: Install & Notifications
HelpInstallNotifications.intro: Migrennity works in the browser, but installing it makes it faster to open and lets notifications work more reliably. On iPhone and iPad this is also required for notifications.

install.title: Install
install.p1: Open Migrennity in Safari. Tap Share, scroll, tap “Add to Home Screen”, then tap “Add”. Close Safari and open Migrennity from the new Home Screen icon. This part matters.
install.p2: If missing: If you don’t see “Add to Home Screen”, you’re probably not in Safari. Copy the link, open Safari, paste it there, and try again.

notifications.title: Turn on notifications
notifications.p1: Notifications work only for the Home Screen version, not for a normal Safari tab. First install, then open Migrennity from the Home Screen icon, then go to Settings in Migrennity and tap “Enable notifications”.
notifications.p2: Note: If iOS never shows the permission popup, update iOS, reinstall to Home Screen, and try again from the Home Screen app.

troubleshooting.title: Troubleshooting
troubleshooting.p1: The most common issue is opening Migrennity in Safari instead of from the Home Screen icon. Remove from Home Screen, install again, then enable notifications again.

install.title: Install
install.p1: Open Migrennity in Chrome. If you see an “Install” suggestion, accept it. If not, open the menu and choose “Install app” or “Add to Home screen”.

notifications.title: Turn on notifications
notifications.p1: When asked, choose “Allow”. If you blocked it earlier, re-enable it in the site settings for Migrennity.

troubleshooting.title: Troubleshooting
troubleshooting.p1: If install doesn’t appear, try Chrome, reload, and check you’re online.

install.title: Install
install.p1: In Chrome, look for the install icon in the address bar, or use the menu to install the site as an app. In Edge, use the Apps / Install option. On macOS Safari (newer versions), you can add it as a web app via “Add to Dock”.

notifications.title: Turn on notifications
notifications.p1: When asked, choose “Allow”. If you blocked it earlier, open the site settings for Migrennity and switch notifications back on.

troubleshooting.title: Troubleshooting
troubleshooting.p1: If you allowed notifications but receive nothing, check system notification settings, Focus / Do Not Disturb, and browser site permissions.

microcopy.iosTooltip: On iPhone/iPad, notifications work only after you add Migrennity to Home Screen and open it from that icon.
microcopy.notificationsTile: Turn on alerts and reminders (you can change this anytime).

Questionnaires.msq_q_number_note: Q1–Q14 are the standard MSQ v2.1 item numbers. Domains: Q1–Q7 Restrictive, Q8–Q11 Preventive, Q12–Q14 Emotional.
Questionnaires.msq_copyright_note: We don’t include the official 14 MSQ v2.1 question texts here because the instrument is copyrighted/licensed. This screen uses the standard item numbering (Q1–Q14) for scoring.
Questionnaires.msq_get_official_prefix: To obtain the official instrument text and translations, request MSQ v2.1 via
Questionnaires.msq_get_official_suffix: Once licensed, you can insert the exact wording per locale without changing the scoring.
Questionnaires.msq_blueprint_rfr: Restrictive (Q1–Q7): limitations in day‑to‑day activities (work/home tasks, concentration, energy, leisure, relationships).
Questionnaires.msq_blueprint_rfp: Preventive (Q8–Q11): activities interrupted/prevented (cancelling plans, needing help, stopping tasks mid‑way, missing social activities).
Questionnaires.msq_blueprint_ef: Emotional (Q12–Q14): emotional impact (frustration/fed up, feeling like a burden, fear of letting others down).

q1.question: Is this medical advice?
q1.answer: No. Migrennity is not a medical device and does not provide diagnosis, treatment advice, or predictions.

q2.question: Is Migrennity free?
q2.answer: Core tracking is free. Optional premium features may be introduced later, but a generous free tier will remain.

q3.question: Can I share with my doctor?
q3.answer: Yes. Share a secure link or bring a clean summary to appointments.

q4.question: How is this different from other trackers?
q4.answer: Evidence-first, conservative insights, validated outcomes, and privacy-first design. No hype.

q5.question: Is my data private?
q5.answer: We never sell data. You control what you share and can delete your account anytime. See /privacy for details.

HelpAiConnector.meta_title: MCP server for Claude — connect your migraine data | Migraine.Club
HelpAiConnector.meta_description: Connect Claude or any MCP-compatible AI assistant to your Migraine.Club account. Ask about your migraine history in plain language and log attacks by chatting. Setup takes a minute.
HelpAiConnector.title: Connect your AI assistant
HelpAiConnector.intro: You can connect Claude, or any other assistant that supports MCP connectors, to your Migraine.Club account. Once connected, you can ask about your own migraine history in plain language and log an attack while it is happening, without opening the app.
HelpAiConnector.what_read: Read your attacks, medication doses, daily diary, computed insights, medication-overuse status and clinician reports.
HelpAiConnector.what_write: Log new attacks, medication doses, diary entries, and triggers or protectors — and correct entries it created.
HelpAiConnector.what_never_delete: It can never delete anything. Deleting records stays in the app, on purpose.
HelpAiConnector.before_account: A Migraine.Club account you can sign in to.
HelpAiConnector.before_consent: Health-data consent granted in the app — without it, the assistant is refused access to your records.
HelpAiConnector.before_claude: A Claude account on a plan that allows custom connectors.
HelpAiConnector.field_secret_note: Leave the OAuth client secret field empty. The connection uses PKCE and does not need one. The client ID above is not a secret — it is sent in the sign-in link and is safe to share.
HelpAiConnector.step1_body: Go to Settings, then Connectors, and choose to add a custom connector.
HelpAiConnector.step2_body: Use the server URL above, exactly as written, including the /api/mcp ending.
HelpAiConnector.step3_body: Put the OAuth client ID above into the client ID field, and leave the client secret blank.
HelpAiConnector.step4_body: Claude sends you to Migraine.Club to sign in. You will then see exactly what access is being requested — read your records, and add new ones. Approve it to finish.
HelpAiConnector.step5_body: Open a new chat and ask about your recent migraines. If the assistant answers with your own data, the connection is live.
HelpAiConnector.try_intro: Ask in your own words — these are only examples.
HelpAiConnector.try_example_read: How many migraines did I have in the last 30 days, and how bad were they?
HelpAiConnector.try_example_log: I have a migraine right now, about a 4 out of 5, and I took sumatriptan.
HelpAiConnector.try_example_insight: Is there any pattern in what triggers my attacks?
HelpAiConnector.privacy_body: Connecting sends the records you ask about to your AI provider so it can answer. Only your own data is ever reachable, and only while the connection is active. We never sell your data.
HelpAiConnector.privacy_revoke: You can disconnect at any time from the connector settings in Claude, or revoke access from your Migraine.Club account. Anything the assistant logged stays in your diary and can be edited or deleted in the app as normal.
HelpAiConnector.trouble_consent_body: Open Migraine.Club, grant health-data consent in your privacy settings, then ask the assistant again.
HelpAiConnector.trouble_nothing_title: It cannot log anything, only read
HelpAiConnector.trouble_nothing_body: The connection was approved for reading only. Remove the connector in Claude and add it again, approving the full request.
HelpAiConnector.trouble_stale_title: It says it is not authorised
HelpAiConnector.trouble_stale_body: Remove the connector and add it again. That issues a fresh sign-in and usually clears it.
HelpAiConnector.disclaimer: Migraine.Club is not a medical device and does not provide medical advice. An AI assistant can make mistakes, including when reading or recording your health records — always check anything important in the app, and talk to your clinician about treatment decisions.
